name: Quicksand
label: Revelation
lede: Four guys out of the youth crew slowed hardcore down, tuned it low, cut a melted candle onto a Revelation seven-inch, and handed the next decade of heavy music a blueprint it's still using.

eras.title: Six weeks to Don Fury's
eras.text: Walter Schreifels had written the songs that defined Gorilla Biscuits and played bass in Youth of Today. With players from Bold, Beyond, Burn, Collapse and Absolution he built something slower, lower and louder, and Revelation put it out before the year was over.

years.h: Quicksand form: youth crew veterans, new tunings
years.p: Walter Schreifels on vocals and guitar, [[Tom Capone|88c3e80c-41b6-48c9-985c-26ad5d026abd]] on lead guitar, [[Sergio Vega|a4256437-7cad-40b7-a135-9767863c90cf]] on bass, [[Alan Cage|65d4abbb-054b-4106-a826-0cb2b306341e]] on drums. [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]] of [[Outface|2fabef87-f53f-4792-b05b-6d54a8517d4c]] plays second guitar at Quicksand's first shows, then drops out.

years.h: Quicksand's debut 7", cut at Don Fury's Demo Demo
years.p: Four songs, recorded in April about six weeks after the band formed, at Don Fury's Demo Demo studio in New York. [[Tim Singer|f59575a6-de2d-4eb3-9d6c-a076dcbcd603]] drew an alternate cover that went unused; the sleeve got a melted candle instead.
years.xp:
One description of the seven-inch that stuck, passed along by writer Anthony Pappalardo: 7 Seconds' New Wind crossed with [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]]. Kids who came for Gorilla Biscuits heard it and started tuning down and slowing down in their own bands.

Revelation's catalog lists a big first run split between black and white vinyl, and the record has been repressed ever since.

years.h: Quicksand's first tour, with [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] and [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]]
years.p: Quicksand's first tour, with Ray Cappo's Shelter and Zack de la Rocha's Inside Out, starts with the van's engine seizing on day one. Revelation's Jordan Cooper pays for the fix, and Quicksand miss their first set.
years.xp: The run went from New York to Buffalo, Cleveland, the Unisound in Reading and City Gardens.

years.h: Quicksand headline the Channel in Boston
years.p: About a year after their debut seven-inch, Quicksand top the bill at the Channel, a Boston room that held around 2,000.

eras.title: The Revelation kids go major
eras.text: Polydor signed a band that had one seven-inch and a lot of word of mouth. Quicksand spent the next three years on tour with everyone from Fugazi to White Zombie, made two major-label records, and split after a show in Hollywood.

years.h: Polydor signs Quicksand
years.p: According to Wikipedia, that made Quicksand the first post-hardcore band to sign to a major. Tours follow supporting [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]], [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]], [[Anthrax|b616d6f0-ec1f-4c69-8a79-12a97ece7372]] and [[White Zombie|cfe572bf-840f-4bed-934a-f69f4b1e90d4]] across North America and Europe.

q: By the time we did Slip, that was our biggest influence.
Walter Schreifels, on My Bloody Valentine
years.h: Slip, Quicksand's debut album
years.p: Quicksand's debut LP re-cuts Omission and Unfulfilled from the seven-inch, with Dine Alone as the single. A [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]] cassette picked up on an English tour had rewired the band.
years.xp:
The list of influences on Slip runs from [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] and [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]] to [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]], [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]] and the [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]]. The My Bloody Valentine tape was the one Walter Schreifels singled out.

Thirty years later the reissue booklet collected tributes from [[Scott Ian|40b0dfb0-d7e7-4a92-b0fa-12ed9af54993]], Thursday's [[Geoff Rickly|132f1d42-4567-4dca-b6e1-3765726f91dc]], Refused's [[Dennis Lyxzén|d7bb37a5-3d48-4a2f-a761-fe66d5cdb409]] and Rise Against's [[Tim McIlrath|157e6a4c-5233-42f8-83f5-e43b0c04641a]].

years.h: Quicksand on the road with [[The Offspring|23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067]]
years.p: Quicksand's touring runs into 1994, with a US tour alongside The Offspring and the Freezing Process single.

years.h: Manic Compression, Quicksand's second album, on Island
years.p: Quicksand's second major-label album reaches No. 135 on the Billboard 200. Delusional hits No. 2 on the CMJ chart, and Revelation presses the vinyl edition.

years.h: Quicksand play the first Warped Tour
years.p: Quicksand are on the inaugural run of the Warped Tour, the traveling punk festival.

years.h: Quicksand break up after a show in Hollywood
years.p: After a show in Hollywood, Quicksand split at the height of their popularity. Wikipedia puts it down to fights inside the band and the grind of never getting off the road.

eras.title: Osaka, Boulder, and the album that never came out
eras.text: Two years apart was enough to try again. They reconvened in Japan, recorded in Connecticut, toured with a rising Deftones, and then the old tensions came back and took a third album down with them.

years.h: Quicksand reunite in Osaka
years.p: Quicksand's first show since the 1995 split is in Osaka, Japan. A Hawaii date after it gets cancelled.

years.h: Quicksand play Boulder, then tour with [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]]
years.p: Quicksand's first North American show in three years, in Boulder, leads to an invitation to stay on the road with Deftones and [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]].

years.h: Quicksand split again, Carriage House album unfinished
years.p: In 1998 Quicksand spent six months recording new songs at Carriage House Studios in Stamford with Steven Haigler. The old tensions returned, the band stopped in late 1999, and the album was never released.
years.xp:
The 1998 run had gone well enough that Deftones asked Quicksand to stay out longer. It wasn't enough to hold the band together. The unfinished album and Manic Compression demos ended up trading hands online.

For the next dozen years, the only way to hear what Quicksand did next was a bootleg.

eras.title: The special guest in Pomona
eras.text: In the gap, Walter Schreifels made Rival Schools, Tom Capone played in Handsome and Instruction, Alan Cage joined Seaweed, and Sergio Vega became the bassist in Deftones. Revelation's 25th birthday got the four back on a stage, and five years later came a new album, Interiors, finished without Capone.

years.h: Quicksand reunite unannounced at Rev25
years.p: Billed only as a special guest at Revelation's 25th anniversary shows at the Glass House in Pomona, Quicksand's original four play together for the first time in 13 years.
years.xp:
The five-song set included a cover of [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]]' How Soon Is Now? The reunion came out of Revelation's own anniversary, the label that had put out Quicksand's seven-inch 22 years earlier. By then Sergio Vega had spent years as the bassist in [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]], the band that had taken Quicksand out on tour in 1998.

Two months later they were at the Bowery Ballroom, and by January they were back on a full North American tour.

years.h: Quicksand back in New York at the Bowery Ballroom
years.p: Quicksand play the Bowery Ballroom, their first New York show in 15 years, then Music Hall of Williamsburg the next night and FYF Fest in Los Angeles a week later.

years.h: Quicksand's first North American tour in 15 years
years.p: Quicksand tour North America for the first time in 15 years, and in August play Belgium's Pukkelpop festival.

years.h: Tom Capone arrested in Phoenix, leaves Quicksand's tour
years.p: Hours before Quicksand's Crescent Ballroom show, guitarist Tom Capone is arrested at a CVS on West Jefferson and charged with shoplifting and resisting arrest, per court documents Lambgoat obtained. The band says he's headed home to work on his health.
years.xp:
The police account, as MetalSucks relayed it from Lambgoat, says an off-duty officer saw Capone on camera putting 43 items in his backpack and pockets, and that he kept walking when told to stop and was taken to the ground. It says he admitted to both charges in his interview.

Quicksand finished the tour as a trio, with Walter Schreifels covering all the guitar. Capone didn't return, and every release since has been made without him.

years.h: Interiors, Quicksand's first album since 1995
years.p: Announced in August with Illuminant, their first new song in 22 years, Interiors goes to No. 1 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

eras.title: Three people, still loud
eras.text: As a three-piece, Quicksand made records faster than they ever had in the nineties. Stephen Brodsky of Cave In filled out the stage for a while, and a new label brought a fifth album in the summer of 2026.

years.h: Triptych Continuum for Record Store Day
years.p: A Quicksand 12" EP on Epitaph, the band's first release without Tom Capone.

years.h: Distant Populations, Quicksand's fourth album
years.p: Stephen Brodsky of Cave In guests on Colossus, then joins Quicksand's live band as touring guitarist, making them a four-piece on stage through 2023.

years.h: Quicksand's Slip at 30
years.p: Boston's Iodine Recordings reissues Slip from the original 1993 masters with a 64-page hardcover book of photos and posters and a foreword from Walter Schreifels.

years.h: Quicksand split a record with [[Hot Water Music|c83907ee-8b5a-4547-8f68-96572243ea7f]]
years.p: The Quicksand and Hot Water Music split comes out through Equal Vision, the label that would release Quicksand's next album.

years.h: Bring On the Psychics on Equal Vision
years.p: Quicksand's fifth album, announced in April with their new Equal Vision deal. Stereogum made it Album of the Week.
